items.q: Find the average value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 8]</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The region on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[6, 8]</annotation></semantics></math> is below the axis: its area counts as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+2</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{8 + 12 + 6 - 2}{8} = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>8</mn></msubsup><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^8 f(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Divide by the length 8.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f(8) - f(0)}{8}</annotation></semantics></math>, the average rate of change, not the average value.

items.q: Find the average value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[2, 6]</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That averages the endpoint values <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(2) = 6</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(6) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Use the area: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{12 + 6}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is the integral; divide by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6 - 2 = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: On <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 8]</annotation></semantics></math>, how do the average value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> and the average rate of change of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> compare?
options: Both are 3.

The average value is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>; the average rate of change is 3.

The average value is 3; the average rate of change is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The average value is 0, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(8) < 0 < f(0)</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Must there be a value <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 8)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(c)</annotation></semantics></math> equal to the average value 3?
options: No: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is not differentiable at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, 4 and 6.

Yes: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(c) = 3</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = 0.5</annotation></semantics></math> and at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = 5</annotation></semantics></math>.
Yes, at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = 4</annotation></semantics></math>, the midpoint.
No: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> takes negative values.

items.q: Find the average temperature from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 6</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 14</annotation></semantics></math> hours. Include units.

mistakes.why: That averages the two endpoint temperatures. Use <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>6</mn><mn>14</mn></msubsup><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{8}\int_6^{14} T(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>6</mn><mn>14</mn></msubsup><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_6^{14} T(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>, in degree-hours; divide by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>14</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14 - 6 = 8</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: At what time <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>14</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[6, 14]</annotation></semantics></math> is the temperature equal to its average on that interval?

Over those 8 hours, the temperature rose at an average of 19.297 °C per hour.

At t = 10, the temperature was 19.297 °C.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(b)</annotation></semantics></math>, the largest value, not the average.

items.q: Find the average value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = \frac{1}{x}</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, e]</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^e \frac{1}{x}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \ln e - \ln 1</annotation></semantics></math> <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1</annotation></semantics></math>; divide by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e - 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f(e) - f(1)}{e - 1}</annotation></semantics></math>, the average rate of change.

items.q: A car's velocity <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(t)</annotation></semantics></math>, in meters per second, has average value 4 on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le t \le 10</annotation></semantics></math>. What does that mean?
options: The car was moving at exactly 4 m/s at the halfway time, t = 5.
The car sped up by 4 m/s over the 10 seconds.
A steady 4 m/s for 10 s gives the same change in position.
The car traveled 4 meters.

items.q: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 7]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>7</mn></msubsup><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^7 f(x)\,dx = 30</annotation></semantics></math>. Which statements are true? Select all that apply.
options: The average value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 7]</annotation></semantics></math> is 5.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(c) = 5</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 7]</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(4) = 5</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f(7) - f(1)}{6} = 5</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find the displacement of the particle from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 10</annotation></semantics></math> seconds. Include units.

mistakes.why: That adds every area as positive: it is the total distance. Displacement subtracts the areas below the axis: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 + 12 + 4 - 1 - 4</annotation></semantics></math>.
Count every piece: the triangle above the axis on (5, 7) adds 4 and the one below on (7, 8) subtracts 1.

items.q: Find the total distance the particle travels from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 10</annotation></semantics></math> seconds. Include units.

mistakes.why: That is the displacement. Distance counts the leftward motion too: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 + 12 + 4 + 1 + 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The particle is at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -3</annotation></semantics></math> meters at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Find its position at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 10</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is the displacement. Add it to the starting position: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3 + 15</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(10) = x(0) + 15 = -3 + 15</annotation></semantics></math>; the starting position is negative.

items.q: At what time on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 10]</annotation></semantics></math> is the particle farthest to the right, and why?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 5</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> starts to decrease there.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 7</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> changes from positive to negative there.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 10</annotation></semantics></math>: the position has had the most time to grow.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> reaches its maximum value there.

items.q: On which interval is the particle speeding up?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(7, 8)</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(5, 7)</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(8, 10)</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 5)</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: A particle moves with velocity <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(t) = 4 - t + 2\sin t</annotation></semantics></math> feet per second, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le t \le 6</annotation></semantics></math>. Find its displacement on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 6]</annotation></semantics></math>. Include units.

mistakes.why: That is the total distance. Displacement is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>6</mn></msubsup><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^6 v(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>, without absolute value.

items.q: Find the total distance the particle travels on [0, 6]. Include units.

mistakes.why: That is the displacement: the leftward motion after <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>3.430</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t \approx 3.430</annotation></semantics></math> was subtracted. Use <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>6</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^6 |v(t)|\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> the particle is at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 5</annotation></semantics></math> feet. Find its position at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 6</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Add the starting position: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(6)</annotation></semantics></math> <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>6</mn></msubsup><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 5 + \int_0^6 v(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>.
Position uses the displacement, not the total distance.

items.q: Is the particle speeding up or slowing down at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 5</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: Speeding up: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(5) < 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(5) < 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

Slowing down: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(5) < 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

Slowing down: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(5)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(5)</annotation></semantics></math> have opposite signs.

Speeding up: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(5) > 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(5) > 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which expression gives the total distance a particle with velocity <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(t)</annotation></semantics></math> travels from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|\int_1^4 v(t)\,dt\right|</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^4 v(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^4 v'(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^4 |v(t)|\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: A particle has velocity <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(t) = 3t^2 - 2</annotation></semantics></math> and position <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(1) = 4</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(t)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: This has <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(1) = -1</annotation></semantics></math>. Add the constant that makes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(1) = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

That starts the integral at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(t)</annotation></semantics></math> <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 4 + \int_1^t (3s^2 - 2)\,ds</annotation></semantics></math> <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= t^3 - 2t + 5</annotation></semantics></math>.
That is the acceleration, the derivative of v. Position is an antiderivative of v.

items.q: A particle moves with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(t) = t^2 - 4t + 3</annotation></semantics></math> m/s. Find the total distance it travels on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le t \le 4</annotation></semantics></math>, without a calculator.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^4 v(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>, the displacement. Split at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> changes sign.

Three pieces each have size <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{4}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{4}{3} + \frac{4}{3} + \frac{4}{3} = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: For the same particle, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(t) = t^2 - 4t + 3</annotation></semantics></math> m/s, find the displacement on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le t \le 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is the total distance. Displacement keeps the sign: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{4}{3} - \frac{4}{3} + \frac{4}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A'(t) = R(t) - D(t)</annotation></semantics></math> is 0 only at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 6</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 12)</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>79.459</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(6) \approx 79.459</annotation></semantics></math> exceeds <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(0) = 50</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(12) \approx 50</annotation></semantics></math>.
